fields.Name: Triads
fields.Summary: Three books sharing a connection that can be named precisely, read from their own files, with verified quotations, a constellation diagram, notebook prompts, rabbit holes, a Lexicon term and a line to carry. Volume 1 of the Scribrarium (32 triads, 96 books).
fields.Procedure: The full instructions of the daily scheduled task as run on 2026-10-25 are kept in the Triomnibus repository at method/triads_prompt_v1.md. Outline: preflight on the Mac (Scribrarium mounted read-only); load the Calibre catalogue; avoid repeats via the Books table; read the Lexicon; draw ~150 random candidates and hunt two companions by targeted searches; state the link in two sentences and rate difficulty 1-5; read each book from its own file and verify every quotation by substring check with a location; write up (Thread, constellation, three book sections with at least two elements each, Where this sends you, From the Lexicon, To carry); deliver PDF to Drive, Google Doc, Grist Sets/Books rows and the Lexicon update; verify.
fields.Sources: Commonplace-book practice: Ann Blair, Too Much to Know (Calibre 5817).
fields.Notes: Retired for now on 2026-10-26, not abandoned; can be rotated back in.

fields.Name: An author and their shadow
fields.Summary: One author per week. Day 1: the author's own work. Days 2-6, through the library's full-text index: who quotes them, who argues with them, who translates or rewrites them, who uses them without credit (recorded as suspicion), and a second own work read in the light of the week. Day 7: the map of who cites whom on Johnny's own shelves.
fields.Procedure: Full text in the Triomnibus repository at method/shadow_prompt_v0.3.md; identical to the daily scheduled task's instructions as switched on 2026-10-25 (night). v0.2 changed author selection to the queue; v0.3 added STEP 1c, the complete capture of every book mentioning the author into the Mentions table. Records: Sets (Method, Author_Week, Week_Day), Books, Shadow_Edges, Mentions, Author_Weeks.
fields.Version: 0.6 (live from the run of 2026-11-21). v0.6: selection rules written into the scheduled task — Author_Weeks 'Idea' = Johnny's wish list, never started by a run; day 7 proposes the next author from the Idea rows (note + draft Day_Plan) but only Johnny promotes it to Planned; Methods 'Active' = method in force, switched only by Johnny and only between weeks; a method runs only once it has a written Procedure; Candidates rows without a Calibre_ID are left alone.
fields.Sources: Calibre full-text index (12,819 formats indexed, 2026-10-25). Moretti, Network Theory, Plot Analysis (Calibre 5420) and Hage & Harary, Structural Models in Anthropology (9870) for the network idea.
fields.Notes: First author: Elias Canetti (chosen 2026-10-25; Kathy Acker deferred to a later week). Hardest category: uncredited use; treated as suspicion with evidence, never as finding.

fields.Name: Lens and specimen
fields.Summary: A week with one book about reading; each day one of its procedures applied to a single book, with a note on what the procedure found and what it missed.
fields.Sources: Sedgwick, Touching Feeling (12221); Felski, The Limits of Critique (9618); Guillory, On Close Reading (9586); Barthes, The Pleasure of the Text (500); Eve, Close Reading with Computers (3802).

fields.Name: News oracle
fields.Summary: One concrete phrase from the previous day's news, searched across the library's full text; the book chosen is the one that illuminates it from the greatest distance in time or field, not the one that merely mentions it.
fields.Sources: Sortes Vergilianae (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sortes_Vergilianae); Adam Smyth, 'pins through paper' (https://adamsmyth.substack.com/p/pins-through-paper).

fields.Name: Margin and Lexicon
fields.Summary: Start from one of Johnny's Calibre highlights or a Lexicon term and trace its occurrences through the library with verified quotations; verified finds can be written back to the Lexicon as checked attestations.
fields.Sources: Ann Blair, Too Much to Know (5817).

fields.Name: Mnemosyne panel
fields.Summary: Five to nine short passages from as many books sharing a gesture or form, arranged without a stated thesis, plus one line naming the gesture. Variant: deformance (reading backwards, nouns only, WordNet substitutions).
fields.Sources: Warburg, Bilderatlas Mnemosyne: The Original (6173); Warburg Institute virtual exhibition (https://archive.warburg.sas.ac.uk/aby-warburg-bilderatlas-mnemosyne-virtual-exhibition); Ramsay, Reading Machines.

fields.Name: Pairs/Doubles/Doppelgangers
fields.Summary: A 2 Week reading method that starts with an evaluation of the literature on the topic - framed from the perspective of a writer, not pure literary criticism.  Then a thorough investigation of the topic as it prepsents itself throughout the scribrarium.  Framed against the Triads readings to tie it to existing readings.
fields.Notes: Perhaps among the best of these, and the triads, we can begin a numerology perspective.

fields.Name: The Bildungsroman
fields.Summary: Bildungsroman from multiple angles.  Particularly interested in looking outside of the standard Western Canon

fields.Name: Reading by Country/Region
fields.Procedure: Each week dedicated to a new country or region of the world.  To plan for this I would like to have a preliminary discussion about the big picture approach to the topic.

fields.Name: A school: precursors to afterlives
fields.Summary: One school, movement or group per cycle, read in time order from its precursors to those it influenced. Each day adds one facet to a working definition of what makes this a movement rather than a list of names. The last day draws the lineage and states the definition, facet by facet, with the places where it doesn't hold.
fields.Procedure:
One school per 7-day cycle, in time order from precursors to those it influenced. Subjects are Author_Weeks rows with Kind 'School' and Method = this row (currently 11 Black Mountain Poets, 12 New York School Poets); they share the Idea → Planned queue with the authors. Each day ends with one sentence, the day's FACET (Sets.Facet); day 7 assembles them.
Day 1 — Precursors. Two lineages kept distinct: CLAIMED (ancestors the members themselves name, from their own texts) and ASSIGNED (ancestors the library's other books attach to the school, by full-text search). Read one precursor text the school cites. Facet: lineage claimed vs. lineage assigned, and the gap. Day 1 also runs the Mentions capture for the school's name and its core members, and records day-7 search terms.
Day 2 — The founding statement: manifesto, essay, letter or anthology preface (e.g. Olson, 'Projective Verse'; O'Hara, 'Personism'). Facet: the programme in its own words.
Day 3 — Place and apparatus: the college, city, magazine, press, gallery or anthology that held it together. Facet: the infrastructure the movement needed.
Day 4 — Membership: who cites, dedicates to, collaborates with or reviews whom inside the group; who sits at the margins (associates, students, women often written out). Facet: where the boundary is drawn, and by whom.
Day 5 — Opponents and neighbours: rival schools, hostile critics, the anthology wars. Facet: definition by opposition.
Day 6 — Naming and canon: who coined the label, when, and how handbooks, encyclopedias and syllabi fixed it. Facet: the name as a later act.
Day 7 — Afterlives and the map. Heirs, again two lists kept distinct: DECLARED (later writers who name the school as theirs) and SUSPECTED (books that use its terms or procedures without naming it, recorded as suspicion with evidence). Then the lineage graph (precursors → members → heirs, with rivals and the margins) and a closing essay: what constitutes this movement, facet by facet, and where each facet fails.
Records: Sets (with Facet), Books, Mentions, Shadow_Edges (relations: Precursor of (claimed/assigned), Founding statement, Published by / gathered in, Member of, At the margin of, Opposes, Names/canonises, Heir of (declared/suspected), plus the shadow relations). Same reading rules, reading notes, write-up and delivery as the shadow method.
